     2	
     3	Reference implementation of a NestJS/React CRM. Serves as the measurement
     4	instrument for LLM agent evaluation.
     5	
     6	## Structure
     7	
     8	- `backend/` — NestJS + TypeORM + PostgreSQL

    10	- `docs/specs/` — implementation-level specifications

     1	# Baseline Backend
     2	
     3	This backend is a NestJS + TypeORM + PostgreSQL service for the CRM baseline.
     4	
     5	## 1. Project Structure
     6	
     7	```text
     8	backend/
     9	├── src/
    10	│   ├── app.module.ts              # Root module
    11	│   ├── main.ts                    # App bootstrap
    12	│   ├── common/                    # Shared errors, pipes, filters, utils
    13	│   ├── core/
    14	│   │   ├── database/              # Data source and migrations
    15	│   │   └── seed/                  # Demo and edge-case seed scripts
    16	│   └── modules/
    17	│       ├── company/               # Company module
    18	│       └── contact/               # Contact module
    19	├── test/
    20	│   ├── setup/                     # Test app and database helpers
    21	│   ├── company.e2e-spec.ts
    22	│   ├── contact.e2e-spec.ts
    23	│   ├── migration.e2e-spec.ts
    24	│   └── seed.e2e-spec.ts
    25	├── package.json
    26	└── tsconfig.json
    27	```
    28	
    29	## 2. How to Start the Project
    30	
    31	### Prerequisites
    32	
    33	- Node.js
    34	- pnpm
    35	- Docker
    36	
    37	### Environment
    38	
    39	The backend reads environment files from the baseline root, not only from `backend/`.
    40	
    41	Recommended files:
    42	
    43	- `baseline/.env.development`
    44	- `baseline/.env.test`
    45	- `baseline/.env.production`
    46	
    47	The default development setup uses:
    48	
    49	- API port: `3101`
    50	- PostgreSQL port: `5434`
    51	
    52	### Start the development database
    53	
    54	From `baseline/`:
    55	
    56	```bash
    57	docker compose up -d postgres-dev
    58	```
    59	
    60	### Install dependencies
    61	
    62	From `baseline/backend/`:
    63	
    64	```bash
    65	pnpm install
    66	```
    67	
    68	### Start the backend in development mode
    69	
    70	From `baseline/backend/`:
    71	
    72	```bash
    73	pnpm start:dev
    74	```
    75	
    76	The API will be available at:
    77	
    78	```text
    79	http://localhost:3101/api
    80	```
    81	
    82	### Optional commands
    83	
    84	Run migrations manually:
    85	
    86	```bash
    87	pnpm db:migrate:run
    88	```
    89	
    90	Run tests:
    91	
    92	```bash
    93	pnpm test:unit
    94	pnpm test:e2e
    95	pnpm test:baseline
    96	```
    97	
    98	## 3. How to Generate Demo Data
    99	
   100	The backend provides seed scripts under `src/core/seed/`.
   101	
   102	### Generate demo data without clearing existing rows
   103	
   104	From `baseline/backend/`:
   105	
   106	```bash
   107	pnpm db:seed:demo
   108	```
   109	
   110	### Reset the business tables and generate demo data
   111	
   112	This is the recommended command for a clean local dataset:
   113	
   114	```bash
   115	pnpm db:reset:seed:demo
   116	```
   117	
   118	### Generate edge-case data
   119	
   120	```bash
   121	pnpm db:seed:edge-case
   122	```
   123	
   124	Or reset first:
   125	
   126	```bash
   127	pnpm db:reset:seed:edge-case
   128	```
   129	
   130	### What the demo seed creates
   131	
   132	The demo scenario creates:
   133	
   134	- 10 companies
   135	- 2 to 5 contacts per company
   136	- mixed company statuses
   137	- mixed industries
   138	- recent `lastContactedAt` timestamps
   139	
   140	### Notes
   141	
   142	- Make sure the development database is running before seeding.
   143	- Seed commands use the active environment configuration, so verify `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, and `DB_DATABASE` first.
